decisions.executionNote: Raise and orient both wrists toward top-down nut grasps, retaining elbow-up continuity. Yellow on left and red on right; final centering will use the next RGB views.
Center the top-down wrists above yellow and red nuts, then descend to a visual pregrasp height; no closure until centering is checked.
Refine centering from wrist images and lower slowly with both grippers open. Yellow needs a larger forward correction than red; checking clearance before closing.
Back off the forward overshoot and raise slightly from table contact, then close around the yellow and red nut flats. Retention remains to be verified by a lift.
Lift both closed grasps and carry each nut above its same-color screw without crossing workspaces. Use ending wrist views to verify retention and align insertion.
Both nuts remain between the fingers. Make small lateral centering corrections and lower toward screw tips, stopping before the first tightening rotation to inspect coaxial alignment.
Correct the visible rightward screw-axis offsets, gently seat the nuts, and attempt a small clockwise threading stroke with closed grippers. Yellow engagement is less certain than red.
The first turn did not visibly establish coaxial engagement. Translate each retained nut toward its screw tip using the rotated wrist view, with only a very small downward seating motion.
Recenter the fingers around the visibly offset nuts and regrasp. The previous lateral correction did not retain a centered grasp, so pause threading and restore secure placement first.
Release and retreat vertically to recover from the slipped, tilted nuts. Reset wrist yaw for a clear overhead view before attempting a fresh upright grasp.
Yellow now appears upright over its screw after release; approach it for a centered tightening grasp. Reposition the right wrist over the separate red nut for recovery.
Descend the remaining short distance and close symmetrically around the upright yellow nut and separate red nut. Preserve the yellow screw alignment.
Turn the centered yellow nut clockwise with light axial feed. Lift the recovered red nut clear, then bring it above its screw for a fresh alignment check.

Release yellow without reverse torque and reset the left wrist for another tightening stroke. Red has tilted in the grasp: center its visible offset over the screw, release, and retreat to inspect how it settles.
Regrasp and add a second clockwise stroke to the aligned yellow pair. Red has settled separately and upright, so approach its new table position with the right gripper open.
Reset the open left wrist without loosening the yellow nut. Lower the right gripper straight onto the centered red nut and close at table-grasp height; verify a level grasp next.
Add another controlled clockwise stroke to yellow. Lift red vertically before translating it above the matching screw, keeping the nut level and the gripper closed.
Reset the released yellow wrist for further tightening. Center the securely retained red nut over the screw axis and descend gradually to initial engagement height, then inspect before turning.
Continue clockwise tightening of the visibly aligned yellow pair. Red is centered but slightly tilted; release it over the screw and lift clear so gravity can settle it upright before regrasping.
Red now rests upright over its screw. Lower the open right fingers for a centered tightening grasp while resetting the released left wrist for another yellow tightening stroke.
Apply another controlled clockwise tightening stroke to yellow and begin threading the seated red nut. Keep both grips closed and axial feed small; check red for slippage afterward.
Release yellow after multiple tightening strokes and withdraw toward the gray screw area. Reset and recenter the open right gripper on the red nut, whose grasp is visibly too far back.
Recenter and lower the right fingers onto the seated red nut before closing. Approach the gray screw with the left hand for relocation to the central handoff area.
Attempt a controlled clockwise red threading stroke with small downward feed. Close the left fingers around the gray screw shaft and lift vertically to verify retention before relocating it.
The gray screw was not lifted, so reopen and descend to a lower shaft grasp. Release and reset the right wrist without reversing torque on the red nut, which remains seated.
Lift the newly closed gray shaft grasp and move it toward the left edge of the central handoff area. Continue clockwise red tightening with a small, progressive downward feed.
The gray screw stayed on the table; abandon moving it and reserve a nut handoff instead. Open and level the right wrist while resetting yaw, leaving the red nut seated.
The red nut sits below the finger-center image, suggesting an overly low grasp. Raise the open wrist to grasp its flats at the proper height, then test a short clockwise stroke.
The red nut now stays centered between the fingers. Complete this clockwise stroke with a small axial feed and release without reversing torque; leave the left arm clear.
Reset right wrist yaw with the fingers fully open, then regrasp the seated red nut for another tightening stroke. Keep the nut axis and height unchanged.
Apply a further clockwise stroke to the centered red nut, with 2.5 mm total axial feed. Hold the left arm clear and inspect thread depth and nut retention afterward.
Release the red nut before resetting wrist yaw, then regrasp at the same centered axis and height. The nut remains upright, but additional tightening depth is still needed.
Let the right fingers finish closing, then add a clockwise threading stroke with 2.5 mm axial feed. Keep the other arm stationary and clear.
Open before resetting right wrist yaw and regrasp for another tightening stroke. Maintain the red pair's current coaxial alignment.
Finish closing around the red nut, then turn clockwise with 3 mm total axial feed. Watch for increased seating depth while maintaining the centered grasp.
Release red and reset the wrist through a wider safe yaw range, without applying reverse torque to the seated nut. Prepare for a longer tightening stroke.
Close fully before applying a longer clockwise red tightening stroke, with just over 2 mm downward feed and continuous elbow-up configuration.
Open the right fingers fully and reset yaw without loosening the seated red nut. Preserve its axis for another long tightening stroke.
Allow the red grasp to close fully, then turn clockwise through another controlled stroke with 2.7 mm axial feed, keeping the nut centered on its screw.
Finish a short red tightening stroke, open and lift clear. Move the left arm only within its workspace toward a central receiving position for the remaining gray nut.
Leave the released red pair undisturbed and move the open right wrist above the remaining gray nut, resetting yaw during the elevated transit. Left waits clear in its own workspace.
Center the open right fingers over the gray nut and descend to a pregrasp height. Use the next wrist image to refine the final table-level approach.
Make a small lateral correction, lower to the gray nut's flats, and close the right gripper. Verify retention and level orientation before carrying it toward the center.
Lift the gray nut vertically and carry it inward above the completed pairs. Move the left wrist back within its workspace to leave clearance for a table-mediated handoff.
Carry the visibly retained gray nut to the neutral center staging area, staying on the right side and above the table. Left remains retracted to prevent arm overlap.
Lower the retained gray nut onto the central tabletop and release it upright for a table-mediated handoff. Keep the left arm still until the right has withdrawn.
Withdraw the open right hand vertically and back into its workspace. Only after clearance, begin bringing the left hand toward the staged gray nut from the left.
Bring the left open gripper to the neutral staging point and lower above the gray nut. Right stays withdrawn; inspect final centering before closing.
Lower the left fingers around the staged gray nut, make a millimeter-scale centering correction at the neutral handoff point, and close. Right remains well clear.
Lift the gray nut from the staging point and carry it into the left workspace above its matching screw. Keep the nut upright and closed in the gripper; inspect alignment before lowering.
Correct the gray nut's small lateral offset and lower toward the screw tip while maintaining its upright grasp. Move the empty right arm toward a safe return waypoint in its own workspace.
Begin clockwise threading of the centered gray nut with a small axial feed. Return the empty right arm along a continuous elbow-up path toward its original pose.
Gray engagement is still eccentric. Make a small correction toward the visible shaft, release over it, and lift to inspect settling. Finish the right arm's small origin-pose correction.
Gray has settled upright and coaxial. Reset the open left wrist and descend onto the nut flats for a secure tightening grasp; keep the right arm at origin.
Close fully on the upright gray nut, then apply a controlled clockwise tightening stroke with about 2 mm axial feed. Keep the right gripper open at origin.
Release the gray nut and reset the left wrist yaw without reverse torque on the seated pair. Preserve the centered axis for another tightening stroke.
Close securely on the upright gray nut, then apply another clockwise stroke with 2.7 mm total axial feed. Keep the right arm and open gripper at origin.
Release the seated gray nut before resetting the wrist for the next clockwise stroke. Keep the matching pairs undisturbed and the right arm at origin.
Regrasp the gray nut and add another clockwise tightening stroke with a small axial feed. Its screw tip is now near the nut face; verify seating after release.
Release and reset the left wrist for one further tightening stroke on gray, without reversing the seated nut. Both other pairs remain untouched.
Apply a final controlled clockwise gray tightening stroke after the fingers close, with a small axial feed. Its screw tip is nearly flush with the nut face; release and return will follow inspection.
Release the tightened gray nut and withdraw vertically with open fingers, resetting yaw only after release. Prepare to return the left arm to origin without disturbing any pair.
All three pairs remain upright after release. Move the empty left wrist to its return waypoint while preserving elbow-up continuity and keeping both grippers open.
Return the left arm along the reverse of the safe elevated approach, maintaining elbow-up continuity. Keep both grippers open and leave all three assembled pairs undisturbed.
